title: Ali ibn Abi Talib
hookLine: the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law, brave, learned and plain-living

cards: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, goes to his daughter Fatimah's house and asks where her husband is. They had words, she says, and he went out.
The Prophet sends a man to look, and word comes back: he's asleep in the mosque. So the Prophet goes to him, and finds him on the floor, his cloak slipped off and his side covered in dust.
He sits down and wipes the dust off him, saying: get up, Abu Turab. Get up, father of dust. The man on the floor is Ali, his cousin.
The narrator in Bukhari adds: of all his names, it was the one Ali loved best.

teach.b: Ali ibn Abi Talib was the son of Abu Talib, the uncle who raised and protected the Prophet.
Ibn Ishaq tells that he grew up in the Prophet's house, and he later married his daughter Fatimah: family twice over, cousin and son-in-law. And he was remembered as the lion.
At Khaybar, Sahih Muslim reports, he went out to fight singing a line about himself: I am the one my mother named Haydar.
Haydar is a name for a lion, and tradition also calls him the lion of God. But the tradition pairs that courage with learning.
When the Prophet left him behind in Medina during the march to Tabuk, Ali was upset to stay with the women and children.
And the Prophet said, in Bukhari: are you not content to be to me as Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me?
Another hadith, in Tirmidhi, has the Prophet say: I am the house of wisdom, and Ali is its door. Scholars debate its chain, and Shia Muslims hold it dear. Then there's the plain living.
Abu Turab, father of dust, was a teasing name for a man asleep on a mosque floor, and he loved it. Here is where Muslims differ. Sunni Muslims honor Ali as the fourth of the rightly guided caliphs.
Shia Muslims hold him to be the first Imam, the rightful leader after the Prophet.
Both honor him. A week that opened with Abu Bakr in the mosque ends with Ali asleep on its floor.

how: Muslims honor Ali ibn Abi Talib; Sunni Muslims count him the fourth caliph, and Shia Muslims hold him to be the first Imam, the Prophet's rightful successor.

wordCard.voice: Abu Turab, father of dust, the name the Prophet gave Ali after finding him asleep on the mosque floor, and the one Ali loved best. Today's word.
